title: Whole Grain Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Poultry

content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain pasta with tomato sauce and pieces of poultry is a restaurant menu item (3652). Whole grain pasta retains bran and germ, making it more nutritious than refined white pasta. The tomato sauce is made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil, garlic and basil, while chicken or turkey adds protein and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain pasta contains more fiber and micronutrients than regular refined pasta.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, which becomes more bioavailable after cooking.
The combination of carbs from pasta and protein from poultry provides lasting satiety.
Traditional Italian tomato sauce is simmered for 30–60 minutes to develop flavor.
Poultry is usually seared to a golden crust, preserving juiciness and adding savory notes.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole grain pasta provides soluble and insoluble fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: The pasta delivers a steady release of glucose, offering sustained energy.

items.title: Lycopene from tomatoes
items.content: Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant that may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Protein from poultry
items.content: Chicken or turkey offers high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Prepared with a modest amount of olive oil, the dish remains heart‑friendly.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole grain pasta contains gluten, so individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should choose a gluten‑free alternative.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Tomato sauce can be salty; monitor added salt to keep sodium intake in check.

items.title: Foodborne bacteria
items.content: Poultry must be fully cooked to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While balanced, portion size should be controlled to avoid excess calories.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta hot, tossed with tomato sauce and poultry pieces. Garnish with fresh basil, grated Parmesan, or a drizzle of olive oil for extra flavor. It pairs well with a light green salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat with a splash of water or broth to restore texture. Only the sauce can be frozen; keep pasta separate.
